By the time group business reaches the sales and catering team, most properties already believe their systems are connected. Room blocks sync to the PMS. Status updates move between platforms. Revenue eventually posts. On the surface, everything appears to be working.


But if you lead group sales or catering, you know that connection does not always translate into coordination. Group business should feel like a growth engine. Too often, it feels like something teams have to manage *around* rather than *through* . The issue is not effort; rather, it is that basic integration was never designed to support how modern group business actually operates.


#### **What “Connected” Often Looks Like in Practice**


Traditional integration focuses on moving data between systems. A room block updates. A status changes. A charge posts after the event. These connections are useful, but they are limited. They do not help teams understand what is happening across the lifecycle of a group or how decisions in one area affect outcomes in another.


Group business is dynamic. Pickup changes. Event details evolve. Opportunities extend beyond guestrooms into catering, outlets, and on‑property experiences. When systems are only loosely connected, teams become the glue holding everything together. Updates are tracked manually. Questions are resolved through back‑and‑forth communication. Momentum slows at the exact moment teams need clarity.


#### **The Question That Matters Most**


The real question is not whether systems integrate. It is whether they help teams sell, plan, and deliver group business as a coordinated strategy. When systems only exchange information, teams are left to interpret and reconcile it. When systems support shared workflows, teams operate with confidence.


This distinction becomes more important as group business grows in complexity and value. Speed matters. Visibility matters. The ability to respond to change without disruption matters. Basic integration rarely delivers on those needs.


#### **What Changes When Systems Work as a Foundation**


When Sales and Catering and the PMS operate as part of a coordinated foundation, the impact goes beyond efficiency. Sales teams respond faster because availability and group details are clear. Catering and operations work from current information rather than assumptions. Finance sees a cleaner path from forecast to actual performance.


Most importantly, teams spend less time managing workarounds and more time focused on delivering value. Group business moves forward with fewer interruptions because updates flow through the operation rather than around it.


If your current setup still relies on duplicate entry, delayed visibility, or manual reconciliation, it may be functioning as designed. That does not mean it is supporting what your business needs next.


#### **What Winning Looks Like for Group Sales Leaders**


The most effective Directors of Sales are not asking whether their systems integrate. They are asking whether their systems help them grow group revenue, protect margins, and guide execution from inquiry through the stay. When technology supports those goals, it becomes an operational advantage rather than a maintenance burden.


Group technology should reduce friction, not introduce it. It should help teams move faster without sacrificing accuracy. It should support better decisions while there is still time to act.


#### **How Agilysys Sales & Catering Supports This Shift**


Agilysys Sales & Catering is designed to help group business operate as a connected workflow rather than a series of handoffs between systems.


- Realtime integration to Agilysys PMS solutions at no additional charge
- Direct posting to PMS from S&C for all banquet checks
- Direct posting of deposits to PMS from S&C


Instead of treating Sales and Catering and the PMS as separate tools that occasionally exchange data, it brings group sales, event execution, and property operations into closer alignment.


This approach gives teams a stronger foundation to respond quickly, manage change with confidence, and understand total group value as it develops. When technology is designed for the pace and complexity of group business, teams are no longer managing friction. They are focused on winning the right business and delivering it well.
